task.description: Hard gate on test coverage for REQ-071's 7 acceptance criteria (AC1-AC5 are test-coverage items; AC6/AC7 are not). Ordering note: Step 3 (TEST-DESIGNER) was effectively merged into Step 2a for this run -- the design doc (req071-mount-auth-tenant-status-plugs.md SS3) fully specified all five e2e test cases in exact detail, and ELIXIR-DEV wrote them as real passing ExUnit code in the same Step 2a commit (6e2a1b6) that did the moduledoc edits, rather than a separate TEST-DESIGNER pass. This is a deliberate deviation, not an oversight. Independently verify the tests that now exist actually satisfy AC1-AC5 completely, with no skipped coverage and isolated fixtures, exactly as this gate always does regardless of which agent authored the tests.

result.summary:
ORDERING NOTE (per task description, restated here for the record): Step 3/TEST-DESIGNER was merged into Step 2a for this run -- ELIXIR-DEV wrote all 5 e2e tests directly from the design doc's SS3 exact specifications in commit 6e2a1b6, with no separate TEST-DESIGNER handoff. Gate applied unchanged regardless.

Re-read docs/requirements.yaml's REQ-071 entry verbatim: confirmed 7 acceptance criteria (AC1-AC7), matching the design doc's own SS1a correction of this run's Step 00 handoff -- the correction is accurate.

Test-to-AC mapping (all real, none placeholder/commented/skipped):
- AC1 (401 + zero Repo queries, no Authorization header) -> test/letflow/router_test.exs 'REQ-071 AC1' describe block. Uses a named telemetry handler on [:letflow,:repo,:query], filtered to self()==test_pid, attach/detach via try/after. Asserts status 401, error body, and refute_received :query_fired. Real assertion, not inspection.
- AC2 (valid token reaches handler, auth_context populated, end-to-end) -> api_pipeline_integration_test.exs 'REQ-071 AC2' describe block. Real tenant via insert_tenant_for_realm!, real Letflow.Router.call/2, asserts conn.assigns.auth_context.{tenant_id,roles,user_id} and status 404 (stub, not 401/403/500/503).
- AC3 (GET /health 200 while OIDC provider worker down) -> router_test.exs 'REQ-071 AC3' describe block. Actually kills Letflow.Oidc.DefaultProvider (Process.exit + monitor + assert_receive DOWN + refute Process.alive?) before calling /health, then asserts 200. Genuinely exercises the failure condition, not a mocked stand-in.
- AC4 (migrating tenant: POST 503+Retry-After, GET substituted-assertion) -> api_pipeline_integration_test.exs 'REQ-071 AC4' describe blocks (2). POST half literally satisfies AC4. GET half is the flagged substitution (see judgment below).
- AC5 (concurrent isolation of a tenant-status lookup failure) -> api_pipeline_integration_test.exs 'REQ-071 AC5' describe block.

Re-ran tests myself (not copying step-02d's/step-02a's reported counts): `mix test test/letflow/router_test.exs` -> Result: 17 passed, 0 failures. `mix test test/letflow/plugs/api_pipeline_integration_test.exs` -> Result: 4 passed, 0 failures. Combined single invocation (`mix test test/letflow/router_test.exs test/letflow/plugs/api_pipeline_integration_test.exs`) -> Result: 21 passed, 0 failures (17+4=21, self-consistent). This reconciles the '17+21=well over 41' framing in my task brief: the real total across these two files is 21, not a larger number -- there is no discrepancy once actually measured, and this is the number to carry forward, not any prior report.

Isolation/self-sufficiency: api_pipeline_integration_test.exs uses `use Letflow.DataCase, async: false` (module docstring explains why: :auto sandbox mode, real committed Postgres state that per-test transaction rollback does not cover -- this is a deliberate, explained choice, not an oversight, matching auth_pipeline_test.exs's established precedent). Every tenant is created via unique_slug/1 (System.unique_integer([:positive,:monotonic])-based), and insert_tenant!/1 registers on_exit cleanup that drops the tenant's schema and deletes its tenant_schemas/registrations/tenants rows -- confirmed by reading the fixture code directly, not by trusting the moduledoc's claim. No shared hardcoded tenant id/slug across tests. router_test.exs's two new tests run under that file's pre-existing `async: true` module setting: AC1's test only attaches/detaches its own telemetry handler (scoped by a fresh make_ref() and a self()==test_pid guard) so it cannot cross-contaminate a concurrently running test in the same or another async module; AC3 kills a real global singleton process (Letflow.Oidc.DefaultProvider) but I confirmed (a) Letflow.Supervisor's :one_for_one strategy auto-restarts it, and (b) grepped every test file referencing TokenVerifier/DefaultProvider -- all auth-touching tests (auth_pipeline_test.exs, authorization_test.exs, etc.) go through Letflow.Oidc.TokenVerifierDouble, a pure-Elixir double (read test/support/token_verifier_double.ex directly) that never calls the real Oidcc worker -- so no sibling test anywhere in the suite depends on that process's liveness during the brief kill/restart window. No hardcoded secrets/connection strings found in either file ("valid-test-token" is TokenVerifierDouble's documented test sentinel, not a real credential). Tests are order-independent: each creates its own tenant/state and does not read state left by another test.

Judgment call 1 -- AC2/AC4-GET substituted assertions: ACCEPTABLE, not a cop-out. Read the actual test bodies (not just the design doc's prose). Both assert a specific, falsifiable set of properties that only hold if the full plug chain actually ran correctly: AC2 asserts status is exactly 404 (the stub's own not_found, distinguishable from 401/403/500/503 which is what a broken chain would produce) AND that conn.assigns.auth_context carries the exact expected shape threaded all the way through Letflow.Router.call/2 (not unit-tested against the plug alone -- this is the literal 'end-to-end through the real router' AC2 demands). A wrong implementation (auth not actually mounted, or mounted in the wrong order, or not attaching assigns) would fail this test with a 401/403/500 or a KeyError on conn.assigns.auth_context, so it discriminates real behavior. AC4-GET similarly asserts status 404 (not 503), refute of the Retry-After header, and documents in its own comment exactly why a bare telemetry refute_received would be dishonest (AuthPipeline's own JIT-provisioning queries fire first in the same request, so a naive 'zero queries' assertion would be either spuriously failing or require scoping logic the test correctly declines to fake) -- it relies instead on the behavioral proof (404 not 503, no Retry-After) which is sufficient given TenantStatus's call/2 has exactly one Repo-touching code path (check_write_pause/2) and the passing status assertion already proves that path was not taken. Both tests' own comments state explicitly, in-line, that they substitute for AC2's/AC4's literal wording and why -- this was already correctly flagged as a requirement-wording gap by CODE-DESIGNER (design doc SS1, AC2 and AC4 sections) and independently reported to ORCH as a finding rather than silently resolved, and CODE-DESIGN-VALIDATOR already concurred at Step 1b. I independently re-derive the same conclusion from the test code itself, not from re-reading their agreement: given REQ-070 deliberately left all ten sub-routers as 404-only stubs (out of REQ-071's scope to fix), no test against a real mounted route can produce a literal 200 without fabricating a fake production route, which the task explicitly forbids -- so demanding the literal wording would force either scope creep or busywork. No new issue required beyond what SS1/Step 1b already surfaced (open question 2 in the design doc's SS7, already logged) -- not re-filing a duplicate.

Judgment call 2 -- AC5 concurrency soundness: SOUND, not sequential-looking-concurrent. Read Test 5 directly: `bad_task = Task.async(fn -> ... end)` is created and returns immediately (Task.async does not block), THEN `good_task = Task.async(good_conn_fun)` is created -- both tasks are genuinely in flight (both processes started and running concurrently against the real, :auto-mode Ecto pool) before either is awaited via `Task.await(bad_task)` followed by `Task.await(good_task)`. This is the correct pattern; the common pitfall (creating one task, immediately awaiting it, then creating and awaiting the second -- which is sequential despite using Task.async) is not present here. The test asserts the bad task crashes with %Ecto.Query.CastError{} (TenantStatus.call/2's check_write_pause/2 has no try/rescue/with around Repo.get/2 -- confirmed directly in tenant_status.ex) and that the good task's conn is unhalted with status nil (TenantStatus passing an :active tenant through unmodified) -- proving the crash in one request's process did not corrupt or block the concurrently-running good request, which is exactly OQ-14's fail-closed-is-isolated guarantee.

AC6 grep re-confirmed independently: `grep -n "Not mounted in front of any route today" lib/letflow/plugs/auth_pipeline.ex lib/letflow/plugs/tenant_status.ex` returns zero matches; both moduledocs now read 'Mounted since REQ-071' with the exact replacement prose from the design doc SS2.

No skipped coverage, no @tag :skip anywhere in either file, no 'TODO: implement test' text present (grepped for both).

Already flagged by CODE-DESIGNER and concurred by CODE-DESIGN-VALIDATOR at Step 1b -- recorded here again only so a future run does not treat this gate's independent PASS as having silently resolved it.
